en: The Discourse on Dependent Origination, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove.
At the Jetavana Grove, together with an immeasurable and incalculable assembly of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, devas, and others.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the community of bhikṣus:
“I shall now proclaim for you the specific meanings of the beginning of dependent origination; you should listen attentively and reflect deeply, for I shall now analyze and explain them for you.”
The assembly of bhikṣus said:
"Indeed, we pray that you will speak; we long to hear it.
The Buddha said:

"What is called the beginning of dependent origination? It means: because this exists, that exists; because this arises, that arises. That is to say: with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form arise; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise; with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. This is called the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. Such is the meaning of the beginning of dependent origination."
"What is meant by the differentiation of dependent origination?
Regarding 'ignorance conditions volitional formations,' what is ignorance?
It is lack of knowledge regarding the past, lack of knowledge regarding the future, and lack of knowledge regarding both the past and the future."
Lacking knowledge regarding the internal, lacking knowledge regarding the external, and lacking knowledge regarding both the internal and external;
lacking knowledge regarding karma, lacking knowledge regarding its maturation, and lacking knowledge regarding both karma and its maturation;
lacking knowledge regarding the Buddha, lacking knowledge regarding the Dharma, and lacking knowledge regarding the Saṅgha.
Ignorance regarding suffering, ignorance regarding its origin, ignorance regarding its cessation, and ignorance regarding the path;
ignorance regarding causes, ignorance regarding effects, and ignorance regarding the phenomena produced by causes;
ignorance regarding the wholesome, and ignorance regarding the unwholesome.
Ignorance regarding what is blameworthy and ignorance regarding what is blameless;
ignorance regarding what should be cultivated and ignorance regarding what should not be cultivated;
and ignorance regarding what is inferior.
There is ignorance regarding the sublime;
ignorance regarding the dark and ignorance regarding the bright;
ignorance regarding the distinct categories; and ignorance regarding the thorough penetration of dependent origination or the six bases of contact as they truly are.

Thus, regarding those various objects, there is a lack of knowledge as they truly are, a lack of vision, a lack of clear realization, and the darkness of delusion and ignorance; this is called ignorance (*avidyā*).
What are the formative forces (*saṃskāra*)?
There are three kinds of formations: namely, bodily formations, verbal formations, and mental formations; these are called formations.
Regarding "conditioned by formations is consciousness," what is consciousness?

It refers to the six groups of consciousness: first, eye-consciousness; second, ear-consciousness; third, nose-consciousness; fourth, tongue-consciousness; fifth, body-consciousness; and sixth, mind-consciousness. These are called consciousness.
"Regarding 'consciousness conditions name-and-form,' what is meant by 'name'?
It refers to the four formless aggregates:
first, the aggregate of feeling; second, the aggregate of perception; third, the aggregate of formations; and fourth, the aggregate of consciousness."
What is form? It refers to all that is form:

all the four great elements and that which is derived from the four great elements. This form and the aforementioned "name" are condensed into one and collectively termed "name-and-form"; this is called name-and-form.
"Regarding 'with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise,' what are the six sense bases?
They are the six internal sense bases:

first, the internal eye base; second, the internal ear base; third, the internal nose base; fourth, the internal tongue base; fifth, the internal body base; sixth, the internal mind base. These are called the six sense bases."
"Regarding 'contact conditioned by the six sense bases,' what is contact?
It refers to the six groups of contact:
first, eye-contact; second, ear-contact; third, nose-contact; fourth, tongue-contact; fifth, body-contact; and sixth, mind-contact. These are called contact."
"Regarding 'conditioned by contact is feeling,' what is feeling?
There are three kinds of feeling: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; these are called feeling."
"Regarding 'craving conditioned by feeling,' what is craving?
There are three kinds of craving: namely, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for form, and craving for the formless; these are called craving."
"Regarding 'craving conditions grasping,' what is grasping?
It refers to the four types of grasping:
first, grasping at sense-pleasures; second, grasping at views; third, grasping at rules and observances; and fourth, grasping at the doctrine of self. These are called grasping."
"Regarding 'existence conditioned by grasping,' what is existence?
There are three kinds of existence: namely, existence in the realm of desire, existence in the realm of form, and existence in the formless realm; these are called existence."
“With what as condition is there birth? What is birth?

It refers to the various beings, within their respective classes of beings, undergoing birth, being born, coming forth, and appearing; the acquisition of aggregates, the acquisition of elements, the acquisition of bases; the arising [of the body] and the manifestation of the life-faculty—this is called birth.”
"Regarding 'birth as the condition for aging and death,' what is aging? It refers to the fading and changing of the hair;

the skin becoming loose and wrinkled; the body becoming decrepit and broken down; the spine becoming bent and the body covered with dark spots; breathing becoming labored and hurried; the physical form becoming stooped; leaning upon a staff; becoming clouded in mind and physically frail; undergoing decline and decay; the faculties becoming senile and matured; functional capacities being destroyed; all conditioned phenomena (saṃskāras) becoming worn out; and the form becoming putrid—this is called aging."

What is death? It refers to those various sentient beings, from their respective classes of sentient beings, reaching their end, perishing, and vanishing; they relinquish their life-span and relinquish their warmth; their life-faculty ceases and passes away; they cast off the aggregates; at the time of death, their momentum is exhausted—this is called death.

This death, together with the preceding aging, is briefly treated as one and collectively termed "aging-and-death. This is what is called the meaning of the specific distinctions within dependent origination.
"Monks! I have thus explained to you the specific distinctions in the meaning of the dependent origination that was initially set forth."

When the Bhagavān had finished speaking this sutra, the assembly of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, devas, humans, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they attained what they had never experienced before, and with faith and acceptance, they put it into practice.
The Discourse on Dependent Origination, one fascicle.
